PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 77 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 08/14/25 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of lower extremity edema, and assessment of fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit to assess his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and ongoing fatigue. Since his last visit, Mr. Fairfax reports a slight improvement in his respiratory symptoms, with decreased frequency of morning wheezing episodes. He attributes this improvement to consistent use of his albuterol inhaler and adherence to his fluticasone/salmeterol regimen. He continues to use albuterol approximately once daily, and he reports no exacerbations or increased shortness of breath.
However, he notes that his lower extremity edema has not shown significant improvement despite adherence to dietary sodium restrictions and continuation of furosemide at 40 mg daily. The edema remains at 1+ pitting, and he describes a worsening of the swelling by the end of the day. He denies any new symptoms such as pain, warmth, or erythema in the legs, but expresses concern over the persistent nature of the edema.
Regarding his fatigue, Mr. Fairfax reports no change; he continues to feel a generalized tiredness that is not alleviated by rest. He denies any recent weight changes, alterations in appetite, or sleep disturbances. He remains active with light daily activities but finds himself needing to rest more frequently.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - - cough, - sputum production, + mild wheezing, - dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily 4. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain 5. Furosemide 40 mg daily
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 78, BP 130/80, RR 18, O2 sat 94% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.5, Hgb 13.0, Hct 38.5, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 136, K 4.1, Cl 98, CO2 26, BUN 16, Cr 1.1, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 410 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Continue current inhaler regimen. Given the recent improvement in respiratory symptoms, no changes to the medication regimen at this time. Follow-up in 1 month. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains well-controlled. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: As there is no significant improvement, consider increasing furosemide to 60 mg daily while monitoring for electrolyte imbalances. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs when possible. 4. Fatigue: Given the normal thyroid function tests, consider other potential causes such as anemia or deconditioning. Schedule a follow-up CBC and metabolic panel in one month to monitor for any changes.
Patient education reinforced regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to manage COPD and edema effectively.
